Have a look at the places you move through
Six questions, once. Nothing to add up, nothing to buy.
The stairs
Can you see every step from the top and from the bottom, with the light on?
A switch at both ends is the usual fix. Where there is only one, a plug-in light partway down does the same job for a few pounds.
The way to the bathroom at night
If you need the bathroom in the night, is there light the whole way without hunting for a switch?
A small light that comes on by itself in the hall or by the skirting board, so the route is lit before you are properly awake.
The floor you cross most
Are the rugs flat and the cables out of the way along the route you use most often?
Double sided tape holds a rug corner down. A cable can usually go behind the furniture rather than across the floor.
Where you would reach out
Is there something solid to hold at the places you already put a hand out, getting up or crossing a room?
Notice where your hand goes on its own. That is where a rail belongs, and a joiner will fit one in under an hour.
Beside the bed
Is the floor beside your bed clear, with the light and anything you need within reach of sitting up?
The lamp, your glasses and the phone on the side you get out of, and nothing on the floor between the bed and the door.
The way in and out
Can you get out of the front door and back in on your own, at any time of day?
A threshold ramp is a rubber or metal strip that sits over the step and needs no fixing down. Where the step is deeper, a joiner can build a longer one in a morning.
The light where you are
Can you turn the light on and off from where you lie, without getting up?
A lamp on the side you get out of, or a plug-in switch you can keep on the bed. Both cost a few pounds and neither needs an electrician.
The seats you move between
Are the seats you move between, the bed, the chair, the car, near enough the same height?
A firm cushion raises the lower seat and takes the climb out of the move. Arms to push down on do more than a soft seat does.
What you wear indoors
Do you have something on your feet indoors that fastens and holds your heel?
A pair of indoor shoes that fasten, kept by the bed. Backless slippers come off at the moment you would rather they did not.
